label: lem:central
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:central}
Let $A_1=\rho(\sigma_1)$ and $A_2=\rho(\sigma_2)$ be a unitary
representation of $B_3$ on $V_t$.  Put
\[
 X=A_1A_2A_1,\qquad Y=A_1A_2.
\]
Then $X^2=Y^3=\theta_tI$.  Given $\alpha^2=\theta_t$ and
$\beta^3=\theta_t$, set
\[
 Q=\alpha^{-1}X,\qquad P=\beta^{-1}Y,\qquad
 \lambda=\alpha\beta^{-1}.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:PQ}
 Q^2=P^3=I,\qquad A_1=\lambda P^{-1}Q,\qquad
 \lambda^6=\theta_t.
\end{equation}
Conversely, unitary $P,Q$ satisfying~\eqref{eq:PQ} reconstruct a unitary
$B_3$ representation with the indicated central character.
head: environment
name: Central reduction

title: Proof
body_md:
The braid relation gives
$(\sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1)^2=(\sigma_1\sigma_2)^3$.  In a ribbon
category this central full twist acts on
$\operatorname{Hom}(t,B^{\otimes3})$ as
$\theta_t\theta_B^{-3}=\theta_t$, because $\theta_B=1$.  Moreover
$Y^{-1}X=A_1$, proving the forward implication.  Conversely set
$X=\alpha Q$, $Y=\beta P$, and define
$A_1=Y^{-1}X$ and $A_2=X^{-1}Y^2$.  Direct substitution gives the braid
relation and the claimed central character.

label: lem:branchsymmetry
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Branch symmetry

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $D_{b+1}=\zeta_6^{-1}D_b$, a solution $P^{-1}Q=D_b$ gives a solution in
the next branch by setting
\[
 P'=\omega^2P,\qquad Q'=-Q.
\]
Indeed, $(P')^3=(Q')^2=I$ and
\[
 (P')^{-1}Q'=\omega^{-2}(-1)P^{-1}Q
 =\zeta_6^{-1}D_b=D_{b+1}.
\]
Multiplication by $\omega^2$ cyclically changes the $P$-multiplicities to
$(m_1,m_2,m_0)$, while multiplication of $Q$ by $-1$ changes $\nu$ to
$12-\nu$.
The branch coordinate increases by one, so every orbit has exactly six
elements.

label: thm:horn
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:horn}
The spectrum~\eqref{eq:C10spectrum} is incompatible with a unitary
representation of $B_3$ having the ribbon central character
$\theta_{C_{[10]}}$.
head: environment

label: tab:compacthorn
title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:branchsymmetry}, fix $b=0$.  Evaluation of the rank-one
inequalities in exact rational arithmetic leaves the following 17 pairs
$(\nu;(m_0,m_1,m_2))$:
\[
\begin{array}{c|l}
\nu & (m_0,m_1,m_2)\\ \hline
6 &(3,6,3),(4,4,4),(5,2,5),(5,5,2),(6,3,3),(7,4,1)\\
8 &(1,7,4),(2,5,5),(3,3,6),(3,6,3),(4,1,7),(4,4,4),
    (5,2,5),(5,5,2),(6,3,3),(7,4,1)\\
10&(4,4,4).
\end{array}
\]

Only the ten rank-two inequalities in Table~\ref{tab:compacthorn} are needed
to exclude these cases.  In the last column, $a$ denotes the row number of
the inequality and the displayed fraction is its positive gap
$\textup{LHS}-d$ in~\eqref{eq:AW}.  Table~\ref{tab:compactcoverage} records a
witness for every surviving multiplicity tuple.  Thus the tables constitute
a compact exact cover, rather than an appeal to all 10,296 rank-two terms.

\centering

Every listed Littlewood--Richardson coefficient is one and every degree is
$d=0$.}
\label{tab:compacthorn}
\begin{tabular}{c@{\quad}c@{\quad}c@{\quad}c@{\qquad}l}
\toprule
$a$&$I$&$J$&$K$&classical Schubert product\\
\midrule
1 &$(2,12)$&$(6,12)$&$(5,12)$&$\sigma_{(9)}\sigma_{(5)}\supset\sigma_{(10,4)}$\\
2 &$(4,12)$&$(6,12)$&$(4,11)$&$\sigma_{(7)}\sigma_{(5)}\supset\sigma_{(9,3)}$\\
3 &$(4,12)$&$(8,12)$&$(3,10)$&$\sigma_{(7)}\sigma_{(3)}\supset\sigma_{(8,2)}$\\
4 &$(4,12)$&$(10,12)$&$(2,9)$&$\sigma_{(7)}\sigma_{(1)}\supset\sigma_{(7,1)}$\\
5 &$(5,10)$&$(8,12)$&$(5,9)$&$\sigma_{(6,2)}\sigma_{(3)}\supset\sigma_{(7,4)}$\\
6 &$(6,9)$&$(6,12)$&$(6,10)$&$\sigma_{(5,3)}\sigma_{(5)}\supset\sigma_{(8,5)}$\\
7 &$(6,9)$&$(8,12)$&$(5,9)$&$\sigma_{(5,3)}\sigma_{(3)}\supset\sigma_{(7,4)}$\\
8 &$(6,12)$&$(8,12)$&$(4,7)$&$\sigma_{(5)}\sigma_{(3)}\supset\sigma_{(5,3)}$\\
9 &$(7,11)$&$(8,12)$&$(4,7)$&$\sigma_{(4,1)}\sigma_{(3)}\supset\sigma_{(5,3)}$\\

It follows that none of the 217 orbit representatives admits a unitary
factorization.  Lemma~\ref{lem:branchsymmetry} then excludes all 1302 original
tuples, so no unitary factorization~\eqref{eq:triple} exists.

\Needspace{9\baselineskip}
To illustrate the normalization and indexing conventions, expand row~6 for
the first entry of Table~\ref{tab:compactcoverage}.  In the zero-th $\lambda$
branch, take the
$(-1)$-multiplicity of $Q$ to be $6$, and take the
$(1,\omega,\omega^2)$-multiplicities of $P$ to be $(3,6,3)$.  The relevant
alcove coordinates satisfy
\[
 u_6+u_9=\frac16,\qquad v_6+v_{12}=0,\qquad
 w_6+w_{10}=-\frac{35}{234}.
\]
The Pieri product
\[
 \sigma_{(5,3)}\star\sigma_{(5)}\supset\sigma_{(8,5)}
\]
corresponds in our convention to
$(I,J,K,d)=((6,9),(6,12),(6,10),0)$.  Thus the left side of
Equation~\eqref{eq:AW} is
\[
 \frac16-\frac{35}{234}=\frac{2}{117}>0=d.
\]

title: Proof
body_md:
If a unitary modular tensor category realized the candidate datum, its ribbon
structure would supply the unitary $B_3$ representation on
$V_{C_{[10]}}$.  Proposition~\ref{prop:Rsigns} and the fusion rules force its
generator spectrum to be~\eqref{eq:C10spectrum}, while the ribbon full twist
forces the central character used in Lemma~\ref{lem:central}.  This contradicts
Theorem~\ref{thm:horn}.
